draft.title: Varying sentence length
card: A passage of sentences all the same length sounds flat. Mixing short and long sentences gives it rhythm and keeps a reader interested.
it can carry detail, build a scene or follow a chain of thoughts. Example: a sentence that lists what the tide swallowed as it crept up a beach, item by item.
it hits quickly and stands out, so it suits the main point or a sudden turn. Example: "Then the lights went out."

Writers also change how sentences begin, for example with a time word, an -ing word or the subject. This stops a run of sentences from sounding the same. A short sentence after several long ones draws the eye to the most important point.
draft.remember: Mix long and short sentences and vary the openings. A short one after long ones makes a point stand out.

a.q: A writer uses three long, detailed sentences to describe a quiet street. Then comes a four-word sentence: "A door slammed shut." What is the main effect of the short sentence?
opts: It makes the sudden event stand out from the long sentences
It gives more detail about the street than the long ones did
It slows the pace so the reader can relax and settle
It shows the writer has run out of things to say
a.why: After long sentences, a very short one is abrupt, so it draws attention to the sudden event. It adds no extra detail, and its quick, sharp rhythm does not slow the pace.
a.clue: Think about how a short sentence sounds after three long ones.

b.q: Jess writes a passage of five sentences. Each is four words long and starts with "I", such as "I woke up." Which change would best fix the rhythm of this passage?
opts: Join some sentences and start others with a different word
Make every sentence longer by adding the same linking word
Make every sentence even shorter so they are all quick
Keep every sentence the same length but change the topic
b.why: The passage is flat because every sentence is short and starts with "I". Joining some and changing the openings gives a mix of lengths and starts. Making them all longer or shorter would keep the sameness.
b.clue: The problem is sameness, in length and in how each sentence starts.

a.best: It makes the sudden event stand out from the long sentences

b.best: Join some sentences and start others with a different word
